generalCriterionList.description: Tenders  from Joint ventures are not acceptable.

Bidders shall not be under a declaration of ineligibility for
 corrupt and fraudulent practices issued by Government of Karnataka
All the formats prescribed in the bid document shall be filled by the tenderer in complete manner otherwise it will be rejected

It shall be the responsibility of the Bidder to ensure credit of Tender Processing Fee and EMD into the respective receiving bank accounts of e-Procurement on or before the last date and time of bid submission.
EMD Payments through e-Payment mode shall be made as one single transaction and payments made in part are liable for rejection.
Contractors Should be registered with KPWD Class-4 and above Registration
Total value of civl engineering works executed and payments received in the last five years (year-wise)
Bidder should upload List of existing commitments and ongoing work
Bidder should upload List of works for which tenders already submitted
Banker Details

The bidder is required to ensure browser compatibility of the computer well in advance to the last date and time for receipt of tenders. The departments shall not be responsible for non accessibility of KPP portal due to internet connectivity issues and technical glitches at bidders end
Bidder shall pay Contract Management Module processing fees of 0.025% of the contact value (Min Rs.500/- & Max Rs.7500/-) soon after contract has been issued to bidder
The tenderer shall bear all costs associated with the preparation and submission of his tender, and the employer will in no case be responsible and liable for those costs
The cost of the Tender form shall not be refundable
The employer is not responsible for any delay in accessing KPP Portal
All scanned documents to be uploaded shall be in original and the Executive Engineer reserves the right to verify the documents before approval.

In the case of the death of the contractor after executing the agreement / commencement of the work, his/her legal heir, if is an eligible registered contractor and is willing can execute and compete the work at the accepted tender rates irrespective of the cost of the work
The intending contractors are requested to note that they should abide by the detailed instructions and conditions contained in the Standard Tender documents KW1

The successful Tenderer shall deliver to the Employer a Security deposit in any of the forms given Clause 24.1 of ITT for an amount equivalent to 5% of the Contract price plus additional security for unbalanced tenders in accordance with Clause 25.5 & 24.3 of ITT and Clause 44 of the Conditions of Contract.
Materials like steel, cement etc., required for the work shall be procured by the tenderer themselves and should got tested by the quality control authority before use on the work at their own cost.

All the items in the tender including all lead, lifts, loading unloading, transportation, labour, hire charges of machinery curing for concrete works, cost and conveyance of all material and all other such incidental charges necessary for successful completion of works as per the detailed technical specification and direction of Engineer in charge of this work
Contractor should take all precautionary measures to avoid any damage to the utilities during excavation as well as utility shifting. To that extent the contractor should identify the client.
Royalty on construction materials and other taxes will be deducted as per prevailing Govt orders.

As per Karnataka state Government order LD/300/LET/2006 Bangalore dated 01.01.2007 and Government letter no PW/134/BMS/2007 dated 27.07.2007, a sum amounting to 1% of the bill amount will be deducted towards constructions labour welfare fund.
The employer reserves the rights to Reject or accept any or all the tenders without assigning any reasons.
Contractor should follow strictly the prevailing rules of labour act &The contractor should employ only registered labours as per Govt. Circular No. PWD/198/BMS/2009/ Dated: 24-06-2009
Estimate rates are excluding GST as per common SR 23-24 continued to 2026-27 Hence GST will be paid separately for the quoted amount accordingly.

The difference amount submitted by the contractor for the work will be released after successful completion of the work and receiving final bill and the 5% amount (Security deposit) will be released after completion of defect liability period

As per Government circular no: FD 355 EXP 12/2024 dtd 01.08.2024, Letter of Intent (LoI) will be issued in Karnataka Public Procurement Portal 2.0 software, contractor has to accept LOI online and submit the BG s through KPP portal within 20 days. if not tender will be rejected as per Guidelines.
Conditional tenders will not be accepted
The tenderer shall bear all costs associated with the preparation and submission of his tender, and the employer will in no case be responsible and liable for those costs
The contractor shall complete the maintenance works within 3 (three) months from the date of issue of the Work Order or the date of commencement of the work, whichever is applicable.

After successful completion of the work, the contractor shall be responsible for maintaining the road for a further period of 9 (nine) months. During this maintenance/Defect Liability Period, the contractor shall promptly attend to and rectify all potholes, surface failures, settlements, edge breaks, and any other defects attributable to the executed maintenance works, at his own cost, immediately upon noticing such defects or on receipt of instructions from the Engineer-in-Charge, without claiming any additional payment.

Failure to carry out the required rectification within the time stipulated by the Engineer-in-Charge shall entitle the Department to execute the work through any other agency at the risk and cost of the contractor, without prejudice to any other rights and remedies available under the contract.
Accordingly, the total contract period shall be 12 (twelve) months, comprising 3 (three) months for execution of the maintenance works and 9 (nine) months for the Defect Liability/Maintenance Period.

itemList.description: Clearing    and    grubbing    road    land    including    uprooting    rank vegetation,  grass,  bushes,  shrubs,  saplings  and  trees  girth  up  to 300  mm,  removal  of  stumps  of  trees  cut  earlier  and  disposal  of unserviceable  materials  and  stacking  of  serviceable  material  to be used or auctioned,  including removal and disposal of top organic soil not exceeding 150 mm in thickness. By Mechanical Means using Dozer - In area of light jungle ---- With all leads and lifts cost and conveyance of all materials, cost of labour, curing, hire charges of machinery equipment, transportation charges, loading and unloading charges and all other incidental charges complete as per standard technical detailed specification and directions of the Engineer in charge of the work

itemList.categoryName: Vol - 3 -Chapter -16- PANCHAYATH RAJ ENGINEERING DEPARTMENT ITEMS
itemList.description: Maintenance of Drains - The maintenance of drains include erosion, repair, clearing, cleaning,  reshaping,  regrading,  deepening  of  side  drains as well as catch water drains as per technical specification Clause 1908. Ref to MoRT&H : IRC - 1908 ---- With all leads and lifts cost and conveyance of all materials, cost of labour, curing, hire charges of machinery equipment, transportation charges, loading and unloading charges and all other incidental charges complete as per standard technical detailed specification and directions of the Engineer in charge of the work

Maintenance of Earth Shoulder (stripping excess soil) - Stripping excess soil from the shoulder surface to achieve the approved level and compacting with plate compactor. Ref to MoRT&H : IRC - 3003 ---- With all leads and lifts cost and conveyance of all materials, cost of labour, curing, hire charges of machinery equipment, transportation charges, loading and unloading charges and all other incidental charges complete as per standard technical detailed specification and directions of the Engineer in charge of the work

Maintenance of Earthen Shoulder (filling with fresh soil) - Making  up  loss  of  material/  irregularities  on  shoulder  to  the design level by adding fresh approved soil and compacting it with appropriate equipment.Ref to MoRT&H : IRC - 3003 ---- With all leads and lifts cost and conveyance of all materials, cost of labour, curing, hire charges of machinery equipment, transportation charges, loading and unloading charges and all other incidental charges complete as per standard technical detailed specification and directions of the Engineer in charge of the work

Patching of Potholes - Patching of Shallow Potholes using SDBC Gr II 25 mm thick - Patching  of  shallow  potholes  on  asphalt  surfaces  by  using Semi Dense Bituminous Concrete 25mm thickness. The Cost is inclusive of removing the failed materials & cleaning on the road surface, preparation of potholes to the required standards sizes before patching them and application of tack coat at 0.20 kg/ m2 over the asphalt surface including lead, loading unloading, rolling and finishing etc., complete as per specification. ---- With all leads and lifts cost and conveyance of all materials, cost of labour, curing, hire charges of machinery equipment, transportation charges, loading and unloading charges and all other incidental charges complete as per standard technical detailed specification and directions of the Engineer in charge of the work

Patching of Potholes - Patching of Deep Potholes using WBM Gr l & SDBC Gr lI 25 mm thick: Patching of Deep Potholes 75mm thick by restoring the Granular Base  course  using  material  confirming  to  WBM  Grade  -I  with 1ype  Sereenings  standards  wherever  necessary  by  manual means  including  trimming  the  pothole  to  the  required  shape and size, cleaning the pothole, applying Prime Coat (SS1) at 0.70 kg per m2 over the WBM surface and covering the surface with SDBC 25mm thick including lead, loading unloading, rolling and finishing etc., complete as per specification. ---- With all leads and lifts cost and conveyance of all materials, cost of labour, curing, hire charges of machinery equipment, transportation charges, loading and unloading charges and all other incidental charges complete as per standard technical detailed specification and directions of the Engineer in charge of the work
